comparison: Perfect alignment on core mechanistic claims (C32-C34, C66-C67, C80). Both evaluations find the central hypothesis about competing excluded volume and multivalent interactions strongly supported. OpenEval emphasizes integration of multiple evidence lines; peer review highlights this as the main conceptual advance providing 'novel mechanistic insight.'

Perfect alignment on 3D perturbation experiments (C68-C71). Both find these systematic tests of the mechanism convincing. OpenEval details how results support excluded volume dominance in 3D; peer review accepts these as part of 'thorough consideration of various control cases.'

Perfect alignment on 2D perturbation experiments (C72-C75). Both evaluations support these claims showing valency-dependent effects in 2D. OpenEval emphasizes complementary nature to 3D experiments; peer review notes 'great effort' in investigating different scenarios.

Perfect alignment on interfacial tension analysis (C77, C79). Both find the thermodynamic analysis supportive despite limitations. OpenEval acknowledges quantitative limitations but accepts trends; peer review initially wanted more depth but accepted qualitative assessment after revision.

Perfect alignment on computational model design and parameterization (C35-C43). Both strongly support the model development. OpenEval details calibration to experimental data; peer review explicitly praises 'very careful' development with 'strong reliance on binding valency and geometry, experimentally measured affinities.'

Perfect alignment on comparison to experimental observations (C83-C84). Both find the simulation-experiment consistency well-supported. OpenEval notes C84 remains somewhat speculative about sufficiency; peer review affirms successful recapitulation without challenging the interpretation.

Strong alignment on interaction network analysis (C57-C63) with additional spatial organization claims (C64-C65) in peer review grouping. Both find the quantitative molecular-level analysis thorough and supportive. OpenEval focuses on 10-fold reduction in non-specific interactions; peer review accepts as part of 'thorough analyses.'

Strong alignment on theoretical framework explaining dimensionality effects (C88-C91, C93). Both support the coordination number argument as key insight. OpenEval finds reasoning sound; peer review describes as exploration of 'general physical principles' and a 'conceptual advance.' Peer review also includes broader generalization claims (C104-C105).

Substantial overlap on broader generalization claims (C92, C94-C99, C106) with additional system comparisons (C100-C103) in peer review. Key difference: OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature requiring validation; peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting speculation within appropriate framing as hypothesis. Both acknowledge broad significance.

Partial overlap on simulation validation claims. OpenEval R1 covers comprehensive set (C30-C31, C44-C56) including both 3D/2D reproduction and CaMKII activation controls; peer R1 focuses on subset (C30-C31, C44-C46) emphasizing successful recapitulation. Both strongly supportive.

Partial overlap on CaMKII activation control simulations (C47-C50). OpenEval R1 includes these within broader validation set; peer R3 treats separately as key validation. Both find these controls convincing without critique.

Partial overlap on 2D simulation characterization (C51-C56). OpenEval R1 includes within comprehensive validation; peer R4 groups with other experimental consistency claims. Both affirm successful recapitulation of experimental observations.

Partial overlap on spatial organization analysis. OpenEval R3 focuses specifically on layered distribution and CaMKII orientation (C64-C65); peer R5 includes these within broader molecular-level analysis (C57-C65). Both find the detailed structural analysis thorough and supportive.

Partial overlap on functional context and system comparisons (C100-C103). OpenEval R17 also includes functional significance claims (C81-C82); peer R11 focuses more on broader generalization (C92, C94-C99, C106). Both accept the contextualizing comparisons as supported by literature.
